character.lede: A terraced modern house climbs a lake bank on a fieldstone plinth, with a glass stair tower and a lily pond below. A pool terrace sits beside the loggia, and a reading loft with a telescope tops the house.

spots.line: A daybed, low shelves and a telescope fill the loft.
An upright piano stands among the sofas and armchairs.
A long trestle table and four columns make the loggia.

facts.style: Terraced hillside modern on a lake: a fieldstone plinth lifts the main floor, loggia and pool terrace a storey above a jungle bank and lily pond; a glass stair tower with stone piers, a bedroom floor cantilevered over the loggia on walnut fascias, a dark-timber clerestory, an olive lap-siding den and a pale stucco entry block

character.truths: The Core sits on the breakfast bar in the Kitchen. No television, no kitchen island. The upright piano is in the Living Salon; the telescope is in the Reading Loft. Pool terrace and lily pond outside.

vikunja: QA shot is a sign-in wall
gitea: [note] Gitea Mirror is a different listing (it copies GitHub repositories into Gitea). Name only Gitea. Forgejo does the same job; name one Git host per household.
[note] The listing mentions Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing mentions Actions CI; no runner ships: never show a CI run.
Gitea Mirror is a different app.
paperless: [note] AI features are off by default. If you turn them on they can use a local model.
[note] Office document conversion is not wired up in this build; OCR and archiving of PDFs and scans works.
grocy: [note] The listing is short. Describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes and chores only.
Short listing: describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes, tasks and habits only (catalog)
Upstream demo screenshot shows a dollar total: prices on screen
photoprism: [note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
ntfy: [cloud-link] iOS push goes through an upstream relay setting; Android and web can stay local.
No sign-in is configured: anyone who can reach the URL can publish and subscribe. Keep it on the home network.
iOS push goes through an upstream relay setting; Android and web can stay local.
QA screenshot is an empty app with a notifications-blocked banner (shows the product).
navidrome: Description says "from anywhere" and "works offline-first": paraphrase, remote access is not claimed
Already in 11 of 30 stories: one short of the cap of 12; rotate music beats to mStream, Swing Music and Music Assistant
obsidian: [licence] Obsidian is not open source. Do not call it open source.
[note] An Obsidian MCP entry exists so an agent can read and write the vault.
not open source (catalog: never say so)
listing says private and offline: do not repeat
notes are files on the Core, the app is streamed
cryptpad: Listing says "end-to-end encrypted": banned wording (f-security-guarantee), do not repeat
Collaboration with people outside the home needs outside reach
calibre-web: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
marketplace: Documented default admin credentials (admin / admin123); no QA capture.
libretranslate: [note] Works offline once language models are downloaded.
Listing says "works fully offline": banned wording (sec-offline)
Likely already heavy in the existing stories
baikal: Whoever opens the app first runs the install wizard and sets the admin password
Overlaps Radicale and Nextcloud calendars: one calendar server per household
wallos: [note] Fetches logos for popular services from outside.
aider: [cloud-link] The Hub injects its own model endpoint, so it needs no cloud key. A model override field can point it at another OpenAI-compatible endpoint; leave it on the Hub model. A coding agent is private only on the C
[claims] Never claim parity with a hosted coding model and never a speed figure. Every edit is a git commit, which is the approval step: the person reviews and can undo it with git.
[note] The browser interface is marked experimental upstream. Do not call it finished.
[note] Added 2026-10-15 for the builder archetype: the old cloud-or-developer exclusion lumped it with apps that need cloud keys; this one is wired to the local model.

hoppscotch: Without sign-in, collections stay in the browser, not on the Core

skybro: [cloud-link] Reads outside data feeds (ADS-B, weather). Alerts go to Pushover or Discord.
The map and alerts depend on outside data; the Core hosts the dashboard
Home location defaults to Los Angeles from the time zone until changed
Dark map UI with a welcome dialog
joplin: [note] Joplin Server only; the Joplin apps are separate.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
marketplace: Joplin Server carries its own Personal Use License: not open source and limited for business use.
koodo-reader: marketplace: Listing text says nothing is sent to a cloud service; the reader has outside-calling features (translation, lookup, speech).
penpot: Five containers (frontend, backend, exporter, Postgres, Redis).
QA screenshot is the log-in page: reject.
Listing images show community library tiles: marketing.
audiomass: The Core only serves the page: decoded audio and edits live in the viewer's browser, so "sits on the Core" is false until the person saves a file where they choose
Short description says "audio never leaves the appliance": an absolute; paraphrase
open-notebook: [cloud-link] Supports 18 plus providers including cloud ones. Ollama is the local path.
[heavy] Podcast-style audio overviews need a speech model.
Install form has OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Groq key fields: leave blank; Ollama is the local path.
Podcast style audio overviews need a speech model: do not mention.
Capture shows sample notebook content, not personal data.
dropgate: The QA build shows "Standard uploads are disabled on this server": only direct transfer worked in the capture
"Beyond your network" sharing needs outside reach to the Core
enclosed: Listing and the app's own header say "private and secure notes" and "server never sees plaintext": do not repeat
Overlaps Cryptgeon and PrivateBin: one per household
Notes can carry an optional note password and an expiry
